# /draw

Step 1 of the daily loop, F4. A person draws their answer to today's prompt
here; the screen only exports the drawing into a draft, it does not submit
anything. This is the same `DrawPad` canvas as `/onboarding/canvas` and
`/avatar`, entered from the root prompt-of-day screen and, on the pinned-prompt
path, from a specific wall.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/draw` |
| Router file | `app/draw.tsx` |
| Flows | F4 Daily create and submit |
| Position in flow | step 1 of 5, the draft producer |
| Data calls | one read, `getTodayPrompt`, skipped on the pinned path. No write call |
| Shared surface | the `DrawPad` canvas, also used by `/onboarding/canvas` and `/avatar` |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

The seeded draft means this tile shows a real drawing rather than a blank
canvas. The nine swatches on the tile are `REDUCED_PALETTE`
(`packages/shared-types/tools.ts:69-79`), not the sixteen-plus-white
`PALETTE` (`packages/shared-types/tools.ts:18-42`). That matters: see "The
'full toolset' is not on by default" below. No brush-size row and no fill
bucket are visible either, consistent with the same finding.

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| Read today's prompt, shown above the canvas | `app/draw.tsx:51`, `:113-117` |
| Skip the prompt fetch entirely on a pinned deep link from a wall (C15) | `app/draw.tsx:34-39`, `:67-69` |
| Draw freehand on a Skia canvas | `components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:447-457` (component path per its own doc comment, `:210-212`) |
| Pick a colour, undo the last stroke, clear the canvas behind a confirmation modal | `components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:630-671` (palette), `:701-708` (undo), `:290-317` and `:528-577` (clear) |

| Disable Done with an explanatory label when the unpinned prompt fetch failed | `app/draw.tsx:81`, `:196-201` |

## Data calls

**One read, conditional.**

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `getTodayPrompt()` | `GET /prompt/today` | `backend/lambda/handlers/today-prompt.ts` |

The client method is `src/data/http.ts:115-119`. The screen calls it through
`usePromptStore`'s `load()` (`app/draw.tsx:51`, `:68-69`), and only on the
unpinned path: a pinned deep link from `/family` already carries
`promptText` in its route params (`app/draw.tsx:43-50`), so the fetch is
skipped outright (`app/draw.tsx:68`, `isPinned` guard).

**No write call.** Done does not hit the API. It writes into the draft
store:

```
useDraftStore.getState().setDraft({ imageRef, promptId, channelId, strokes })
```

at `app/draw.tsx:94-99`, then pushes to `/story-select` (`app/draw.tsx:100`).
`channelId` is set only on the pinned path (`app/draw.tsx:97`); the unpinned
path leaves it `undefined` because `/draw` does not yet know the
destination wall, per the store's own comment
(`src/stores/useDraftStore.ts:23-27`). That choice happens later, in
`/choose-channels`.

The drawing does not travel as a route param on purpose: a data URI is too
large and unreliable to pass through the router, per the same comment
(`src/stores/useDraftStore.ts:23-25`). That is what makes the draft guard on
the four screens after this one possible.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** `useAuthStore`'s `hydrated` and `currentUser`
(`app/draw.tsx:53-54`), gating the whole screen. `usePromptStore`'s `data`
and `error` on the unpinned path (`app/draw.tsx:51`); route params
`promptId`, `promptText`, `channelId` on the pinned path
(`app/draw.tsx:43-49`).

**Writes on exit.** `imageRef`, `promptId`, `strokes`, and (pinned only)
`channelId` into `useDraftStore` (`app/draw.tsx:94-99`). `strokes` is
best-effort; the PNG is what the rest of the flow relies on
(`components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:339-357`).

No mount-time step marker is written here, unlike the onboarding twin's
`useOnboardingStep` -- this is the production loop, not a resumable
first-run sequence.

## Components

| Component | Path |
|-----------|------|
| `DrawPad`, the shared canvas and its tool row | `components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx`, imported at `app/draw.tsx:7` |
| `DrawingCanvas`, the Skia surface, platform-resolved | `components/canvas/DrawingCanvas.tsx` for web, `.native.tsx` for native |
| `ScribbleUndoIcon`, `ScribbleTrashIcon` | `components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:7` |

`DrawPad` is shared with `/onboarding/canvas` and `/avatar`
(`components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:210-212`), so any change lands on three
screens across three flows: F2, F4, and F8.

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### The "full toolset" is not on by default, and this screen proves it

The task framing going into this page was that `/draw` gets the full
toolset (all brush sizes, the fill bucket) where onboarding gets a reduced
palette. That is not what the source does. `DrawPad`'s `toolset` prop
defaults to `activeToolset()` (`components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:223`,
`src/config/features.ts:27-29`), which resolves to the reduced
configuration -- one brush size, no fill, no clear-vs-fill distinction --
unless `EXPO_PUBLIC_FULL_TOOLSET=1` is set
(`src/config/features.ts:16-24`, `packages/shared-types/tools.ts:150-181`).
`app/draw.tsx` never passes a `toolset` override, so by default it renders
the exact same brush-size and fill-tool absence as `/onboarding/canvas`.
The only real difference between the two screens today is the colour
palette: `/draw` passes no `allowedColors`, so it shows the full 8-swatch
`REDUCED_PALETTE` plus the white "eraser" swatch
(`packages/shared-types/tools.ts:69-79`), while onboarding narrows that same
palette further via its own `allowedColors`. The capture tile confirms
this: nine swatches, no size selector, no fill bucket. Flip
`EXPO_PUBLIC_FULL_TOOLSET=1` and both screens gain the six-size selector and
the fill bucket together, not just this one. Whoever plans against "the
full canvas experience" should plan against the flag, not against this
route.

### The drawing is finalized here, out loud, before submission exists

The write and choose-channels screens both carry the line "your drawing is
final once it's out there -- captions you can still tweak," and that framing
starts here: the raster PNG is committed the moment Done runs
(`components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:325-357`), two screens before the drawing is
actually submitted to anyone. `strokes` is a best-effort side record with no
replay UI yet (see the `onboarding-canvas` page's own note on this). Nothing
about `/draw` lets a person come back and redraw once they have moved on --
that has to be a conscious product decision, not an artifact of what got
built first.
